arguments.command:
python3 << 'PY'
import statistics

# From the table "Composition of the Interest-Bearing Public Debt"
# Data points from December 1941 to December 1942 (end of fiscal month values)
# Row: Dec 1941, Jan 1942, Feb 1942, Mar 1942, Apr 1942, May 1942, Jun 1942, Jul 1942, Aug 1942, Sep 1942, Oct 1942, Nov 1942, Dec 1942

bonds = [
    40000,  # 1941-December
    42078,  # 1942-January
    44305,  # 1942-February
    44847,  # 1942-March
    45363,  # 1942-April
    48157,  # 1942-May
    48776,  # 1942-June
    51765,  # 1942-July
    53680,  # 1942-August
    54413,  # 1942-September
    57285,  # 1942-October
    57931,  # 1942-November
    64868,  # 1942-December
]

bills_certs = [
    2002,  # 1941-December
    2101,  # 1942-January
    2002,  # 1942-February
    1652,  # 1942-March
    3460,  # 1942-April
    3764,  # 1942-May
    5604,  # 1942-June
    6759,  # 1942-July
    8873,  # 1942-August
    10829, # 1942-September
    11336, # 1942-October
    12882, # 1942-November
    17161, # 1942-December
]

print("Number of data points:", len(bonds), len(bills_certs))

# Compute Pearson correlation coefficient manually
n = len(bonds)
mean_bonds = statistics.mean(bonds)
mean_bills = statistics.mean(bills_certs)

print(f"Mean bonds: {mean_bonds}")
print(f"Mean bills: {mean_bills}")

# Covariance
cov = sum((b - mean_bonds) * (c - mean_bills) for b, c in zip(bonds, bills_certs)) / (n - 1)

# Standard deviations
stdev_bonds = statistics.stdev(bonds)
stdev_bills = statistics.stdev(bills_certs)

print(f"Stdev bonds: {stdev_bonds}")
print(f"Stdev bills: {stdev_bills}")
print(f"Covariance: {cov}")

# Pearson correlation
r = cov / (stdev_bonds * stdev_bills)
print(f"\nPearson r = {r}")
print(f"Rounded to thousandths: {round(r, 3)}")

# Also verify with statistics module
r_check = statistics.correlation(bonds, bills_certs)
print(f"statistics.correlation check: {r_check}")
PY
